# Pulse

> Minimalist, high-performance macOS memory monitor and command palette.

Pulse is an open-source native macOS menu bar utility built in SwiftUI that provides real-time system memory monitoring, Chrome tab inspection, and instant process quitting. It runs with an ultra-lightweight ~13.5 MB background RAM footprint and zero idle CPU usage.

## Quick Installation
Run in terminal:
`curl -fsSL https://pulse0.app/install.sh | bash`

Direct DMG download:
https://github.com/Suraj1089/pulse/releases/latest/download/Pulse.dmg

## Core Capabilities
- **Real-Time Memory Telemetry**: Direct kernel page reading via Mach host statistics (`host_statistics64`), identical to `vm_stat`.
- **System Memory Pressure**: Hardware pressure source monitoring (`DispatchSource.makeMemoryPressureSource`) tracking Low, Medium, and High pressure states.
- **Process Memory Aggregation**: Deep memory accounting using `proc_pid_rusage` (`phys_footprint`) that sums nested helper and renderer processes under their parent application.
- **Google Chrome Tab Inspection**: Derives per-tab memory consumption and enables closing heavy tabs directly from the command palette.
- **Instant Force Quit**: Holding the ⌥ Option key dynamically converts Quit actions into kernel-level `SIGKILL` (`NSRunningApplication.forceTerminate()`).
- **Minimal Overhead**: Dormant in the menu bar using only ~13.5 MB RAM; completely prevents the macOS AutoFill daemon process from spawning.
